p01.why: A return statement in a deduced function must not return a braced list.

p02.why: Returning a call of a void function gives void.

p03.why: auto drops references and top-level const, and auto& keeps const.

p04.why: f returns int&& to a local that no longer exists, and reading it in the static_assert is undefined, which constant evaluation rejects.

p05.why: A later declaration cannot write the deduced type int in place of auto.

p06.why: The returns agree, and no return, return;, and return of a void call all give void.

p07.why: The return in the discarded branch does not count, so f returns int and converts to int (*)().

p08.why: The recursive call comes after return 1 fixes the type as int; fact(5) is 120.

p09.why: The recursive call comes before any return statement gives the type.

p10.why: return; gives void and return 1 gives int.

p11.why: The local name is an xvalue in a return, so it cannot initialize the deduced lvalue reference.

p12.why: decltype(auto) gives int for a name, int& for a parenthesized global, and int&& for an xvalue.

p13.why: The returns give int and double.

p14.why: The two declarations use different return types, auto and int.

p15.why: total calls step, a later member whose return type is not yet known.

p16.why: A virtual function cannot have a deduced return type.

p17.why: s has static storage, so (s) stays an lvalue and the type is int&.

p18.why: The result refers to a dead local, and AddressSanitizer stops the read on GCC and Clang.

p19.why: A parenthesized local gives int&& and a parenthesized global gives int&; the types alone are valid.

p20.why: The call follows the definition, and both declarations write auto.

p21.why: Every declaration writes the same placeholder.

p22.why: f is called before its definition gives the return type.

p23.why: A reference placeholder return type needs a return statement with an expression.
